target.name: Eukaryotic Translation Termination
target.description: Protein synthesis ends when a stop codon reaches the ribosomal A site, and this step converts a stalled elongation complex into a released polypeptide and recyclable subunits. Accurate termination sets the true C-terminus of every protein; failure to terminate causes readthrough into 3' untranslated sequence, extended and often misfolded products, and it is the same recognition event that triggers surveillance of premature stop codons.

target.name: cell development
target.description: This grouping describes cell development in the sense of progenitor specification and differentiation within developing tissues, where signalling gradients assign identity and transcription factors lock it in. Wnt output dominates: AXIN2 reports and restrains pathway activity, SFRP2 sequesters Wnt ligands extracellularly, and ASCL2 is a Wnt-driven factor that maintains intestinal stem cells alongside CDX2, the master regulator of posterior gut identity.

target.name: alpha-ketoglutarate transport
target.description: Alpha-ketoglutarate sits at the junction of the citric acid cycle, amino acid metabolism and oxygen sensing, and moving it across membranes is what lets different compartments and organs share it. Carriers of the dicarboxylate transporter family take up alpha-ketoglutarate and related di- and tricarboxylates with sodium at the apical and basolateral surfaces of kidney tubule and intestinal epithelium, generating the intracellular dicarboxylate gradient that organic anion transporters then use as a counter-substrate to secrete drugs, toxins and metabolites into urine.
